instruction: The animations on my screen are too fast and make me dizzy. Please slow down or disable the animations to make the interface more comfortable.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

result.command: ANIMATION=$(timeout 10 gsettings get org.gnome.desktop.interface enable-animations 2>/dev/null | grep -c false); if [ "$ANIMATION" -gt 0 ]; then echo "Animations disabled"; else echo "Animations enabled"; fi

metadata.explanation: Task requires disabling animations via Settings > Accessibility > Reduce Animation. Evaluator checks enable-animations setting is false. Uses existing check_include_exclude metric with vm_command_line getter.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly verifies the animation disable requirement by checking gsettings enable-animations setting
Command logic properly translates gsettings output to clear success/failure messages (Animations disabled/enabled)
Metric check_include_exclude appropriately validates the command output with include/exclude rules
Expected values are semantically correct: includes 'Animations disabled', excludes 'Animations enabled' and 'error'
Command is robust with timeout, error redirection, and proper boolean logic
No postconfig needed - animation setting persists after UI interaction
Complete coverage of instruction requirement (disable animations for accessibility)
Practical and feasible - gsettings command works reliably on Ubuntu/GNOME systems
